items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: It was a fellow by the name of John Kornfeld... And they were inseparable up until death. Well, John died first. And my father always kept in contact with his family.

ctx.x: Can you tell us anything about his teaching of drums? Did you ever see any drum pupils come there and hear him give a voice of any of them? Oh, yes. What he did?

Oh, yes. He always started them off first, just as he did with me. He started them the same for his, for some. Then after it would be with the pad because he said it would develop a better wrist on a pad than to try him out on a drum. Oh, wow. Because he had exceptional wrist and I must say, by me and my father, I've never heard anyone roll a drum equally and as smooth as he had. Just about everybody's told us that ever mentioned when they talk about that role. And he believed in the wrist. Of course, it was from…
Did he ever amount to anything as a drummer? I mean, did he go ahead professionally?
